body:
The maintainer reported this bug in chat on 2026-11-17, on the 0.23.0 build:

> Bug; the machine list is not updated from foloder on start. Neither is it updated when refreshed. It instead just errors over not finding the file it needs.. When the files is actually removedd..

What happens:
- At start, the machine list does not show the contents of the machine folder (`assets`, read at run time since #2282, PR #2293).
- A refresh does not update the list.
- When a machine file is removed from the folder, the list still has its entry. The program then gives an error that it cannot find the file.

Expected:
- At start and at each refresh, the list has one entry for each machine file that is in the folder at that moment.
- A file that is removed from the folder has no entry after the start or the refresh. No error shows for it.
- A file that is added to the folder has an entry after the start or the refresh.
- A missing file that the open document or the default machine needs is still refused by name (#2319). This rule does not change.

Not known yet:
- If the list comes from a fixed table in the program and not from a scan of the folder.
- Which control the maintainer used for the refresh.
- If MCP has the same list. If it does, it must follow the same scan.

Related: #2358 (list the user's machines in the Machine library list) is an enhancement and is a different change.

Done means: a test adds a machine file to a temporary machine folder and removes a different file, then starts or refreshes. The list has the added machine, does not have the removed machine, and shows no error.

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post

labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
### What are you trying to do

I picked the shipped grblHAL machine for a setup that posted with Fanuc. The setup kept Fanuc, and nothing suggested the grblHAL post. A `.mch` file cannot say which post goes with it. `post_offer` offers `default_post_for(kind)` only when the current post does not serve the machine's kind, so for every mill the offer is Fanuc. The pairings exist only as comments in `MACHINES`. #1915 and #1918 expect `default_post_for` to map machines to their post, but it takes only the kind.

### How you imagine it working

- An optional key, for example `controller.post: "grblHAL"`, names a post in `BUILTINS`. Without the key, nothing changes.
- `validate_text` refuses, naming the key, a name not in the registry and a post that does not serve the machine's kind.
- When the mounted machine names a different registry post than the setup's, the existing offer banner suggests the named post. Taking it goes through the existing undoable post command. A mount still never changes the post by itself, and a `.cps` file post is never offered over (#343, #388).
- The shipped machines whose pairing is already written down state their post (Tormach, grblHAL/Sienci, TinyG, Makera, Doosan, Haas, the sinker template). The generic ones state none. `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the key.
- `Machine` is `#[serde(default)]`, so an older reader drops the field. That loses only the offer, never a posted program, so I propose no `PROJECT_VERSION` bump.

Question: should this live in the `.mch` file or in a table next to `MACHINES`? I'd choose the file, so a user's own machine can state its post too. Either way it should fit #924's registry move.

**Tests:** grblHAL mounted over Fanuc offers grblHAL, and taking the offer then undoing it restores Fanuc. A machine without the key offers as now, with the existing lathe-over-mill test unchanged. A `.cps` post is never offered over. The validator refuses an unknown name and a post of the wrong kind. Every shipped machine validates.

Not in scope: a `.cps` path in the machine file, or post options in the machine file.

Related: #1915, #1918, #924, #611. I'd like to claim this and open a draft PR once it is triaged.

  law_tests::gizmo_tests::each_triad_is_labelled_with_its_own_offset_name

  law_tests::path_tests::the_path_wears_the_colour_vision_palette_and_off_restores_it

  law_tests::preview_tests::selecting_an_operation_outlines_its_cut_region
  path_lines::tests::the_mark_follows_the_colour_vision_palette_and_the_dim

Suspected mechanism:

The suite mutates process-global cells in parallel frames while
colour-scan law tests read them. Candidates:

- theme::set_current / theme::current: a live OnceLock RwLock, one cell per
  process (crates/ui/src/egui_app/theme.rs); state.rs writes it on each

The parallel run must be deterministic. A fix: guard every read of the
process-global theme / colour-vision cells with snapshot_guard(), or
serialise those suites. Then pin it with repeated parallel runs (goal:
0/30 failures across repeated full parallel runs).

  (>= 3 runs, 0 failures each).

## What happens

The release-tier preflight of the v0.23.0 cut ran on main `93fe3cfd0` (Windows, release profile, `--ignored` heavy lanes). Two heavy-lane tests in `camcraft-motion` fail:

1. `crates/motion/tests/adaptive_hsm.rs:468`, `a_small_helix_rectangle_never_crosses_itself`:
   `assertion left == right failed: one helix per level`, left 2, right 3.
2. `crates/motion/tests/rotary_adaptive.rs:289`, `the_r62_neck_levels_are_hsm_planned_on_microlift_returns`:
   `the skin level stays HSM-planned`. The notes show only the levels at radius 5.700 and 5.200.

The two tests are `#[ignore]`d. The quick and batch gates do not run them.

## Cause

PR #2013 (issue #2004) changed the shared depth ladder. The first level is now one stepdown under Top Z. The old level at Top Z cut air and is gone. This is the intended result of a reviewed PR.

Evidence:

- The rectangle has Top Z 0, Bottom Z -4, Stepdown 2. The ladder is now `[-2, -4]`: two helices, not three.
- The debug twin `level_links::the_helix_entry_is_one_continuous_descent` was updated by #2013 to two helices ("-2, -4; #2004: none at Top Z").
- The r6.2 bar is r6 at most. The level on the r6.2 stock skin cut air. #2013 removed it and updated the other tests in `rotary_adaptive.rs` (`no level on the r7 skin (#2004)`, the `GOLDEN_RINGS` re-pin). It did not update these two ignored tests.

No toolpath behaviour is lost. The expectations are stale.

## Fix

Update the two expectations to pin the new behaviour with the same strength, on branch `cut/0.23-heavy-lanes` (release cut fix, no PR):

- `adaptive_hsm`: two helices, and each helix lands on -2 and -4.
- `rotary_adaptive`: no level on the r6.2 skin. The asserts on the 5.7 and 5.2 levels stay.

Done means: the two tests pass in release with `--ignored`, and the two whole test binaries pass with and without `--ignored`.

title: grblHAL and Tormach posts write G86 with no P when the bore dwell is 0

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
What happens: The grblHAL and Tormach posts write a G86 block with no P word when the bore dwell is 0 (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps` and `assets/posts/tormach.cps`, `onCycle`). Each new G86 block comes after G80.

The LinuxCNC interpreter requires P on the first G86 block of a cycle. `src/emc/rs274ngc/interp_cycles.cc`, `convert_cycle_xy`:

```
CHKS(((settings->motion_mode != G_86) && (block->p_number == -1.0)),
    NCE_DWELL_TIME_P_WORD_MISSING_WITH_G86);
```

The LinuxCNC G-code reference gives the format `G86 ... R- L- P- $-` and lists "a P number is required" as a canned-cycle error. grblHAL follows the LinuxCNC specification for its canned cycles.

Expected: A bore with a dwell of 0 posts a program that the control accepts. One option is `P0` on G86 (the LinuxCNC reference permits a P that is not negative). Check the grblHAL code list for G86 first.

Priority: `P3`. The control stops the program with an error. The output is not a silent wrong motion. The behaviour on a real grblHAL or PathPilot control is not verified.

Evidence: Found during the work on #2360. The G86 goldens of `crates/post/tests/bore_cycle.rs` (grblhal, tormach) show G86 with no P.

Done means: A test pins the G86 P word for a zero dwell on the two posts, and the goldens agree.

## Problem

Siemens, *SINUMERIK ONE / 840D sl / 828D ISO dialects*, Function Manual, 07/2021, section 6.3, table 6-2 (drilling cycles, ISO dialect M) gives the address words of each cycle. Two cycles in `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps` (`onCycle()`) do not agree with it:

The G86 dwell refusal agrees with the table (no P on G86). G82 and G89 agree (P listed).

- G84: the post writes the P dwell, or it refuses the dwell by name with `msg()`. It never drops it silently.
- G85: the post refuses a dwell by name, or it gives a source that shows P on G85.

## Notes

- Do not change behaviour without a source. Use behaviour only from the manual; do not copy its text.
- Check first if the stream can give a TAP or REAM cycle with a dwell above 0.
- Found during #2349 / PR #2353.

body:
## Problem

Four posts drop a bottom dwell on G73 (chip-break peck) and give no warning. The program runs with no dwell. The operator does not know.

Each post has this line in `onCycle()`:

```js
if (ms > 0 && g !== "G73" && g !== "G84") words.push("P" + ms);
```

- `assets/posts/fanuc.cps:1076`
- `assets/posts/haas.cps:913`
- `assets/posts/mazak.cps:902`
- `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps:1237`

The same line drops a G84 dwell without a warning too.

The Sinumerik post has the same pattern. #2354 tracks it, so it is not in this issue.

## Expected

Each post writes the dwell word that its control documents for G73, or it refuses the dwell by name with `msg()`. A dwell is never dropped silently (Prime Directive).

## Notes

- Check the published programming manual of each control for a P word on G73 and G84. Use behaviour only.
- Found during #2349 / PR #2353. The `grblhal.cps` and `tormach.cps` posts were not checked (another worker has them, #2348).

title: Rotary Offset on the Tormach microARC 4: every level that cuts takes two laps of A, so the PathPilot post refuses it (A counts past the -360..360 travel)

body:
Found while writing the continuous 4-axis walkthrough for #1904 (stacked on PR #2342, which posts wrapped A on `tormach.cps`).

**What happens.** A Rotary Offset rough on the microARC 4 machine file does not post once a level meets the part:

```
post blocked - 1 warning(s): A361.862 in operation Journal is beyond the A axis travel -360..360 degrees - A counts on through 360 (PathPilot does not roll A over), so the operation turns too far in one direction
```

**Why.** `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_offset.rs` develops the bar as a cover of two laps plus the seam pad ("the cover is two laps, the seam copy included"); only an air level sweeps one lap. PathPilot does not roll A over (Hub reading 1 on #796), so the post counts A on, and the machine file states A travel -360..360 (kept in PR #2342: "PathPilot's real A limits are an open Hub check"). Two laps plus the pad cannot fit in 720 degrees.

**Repro (on the #1904 branch, before the demo was changed to Rotary Parallel).** 3/4 in round bar as stock (a model, R 0.375 in, X-1.5..0), a stepped model (journal R 0.340 in), 1/8 in ball, Rotary Offset with radial stepdown 0.03 in, any strategy (Auto, Zigzag, Waterline, Offset rings; climb or conventional): each is refused with A between 360.9 and 363.4. With a Box stock and a 0.1 in stepdown the only level is an air level (one lap, A-86.25..273.75) and it posts, but it cuts nothing.

**Expected.** One of:
- the rough's rings close without a second lap (or each ring unwinds: lift, turn A back, go on), so a level stays inside 720 degrees; or
- the machine file states the travel PathPilot really allows, if the Hub check of PR #2342 (step 5) shows it is wider; or
- the refusal says what to change.

**Workaround.** None found: Rotary Offset cannot be used on this machine file today. Rotary Parallel posts (its A stays inside one turn).

Done means: a Rotary Offset rough of a round bar posts on `tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch` with `tormach.cps`, pinned by a test, or the limit is documented with a refusal that names the fix.

- `machine::script_props` (`crates/post/src/post/machine.rs:211-232`) then sets rapid, feed and spindle limits to 0.0 and the coolant list to empty.

Expected: the post is refused with a message that names the missing or malformed machine file (Prime Directive: correct output or a visible refusal).

Evidence: found by code reading in the review of PR #2318 (see the review comment there, and the comment on issue #2316). The exact output text was not recorded. The case occurs only when the default machine file is absent and the posts folder is present.

Done means:
- A post with a null machine is refused, with the file named in the message.
- A test pins the refusal for a missing file and for a malformed file.
- The comment at `posting.rs:173-174` is true.

title: main is red (post-merge gate): the data_dir lookup does not know the new cargo build-dir layout

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## Run

Post-merge gate run 43990986558 (`post-merge.yml`, batch tier, self-hosted Linux runner) on `3f41b8da6b65b8154132878e459d4430e3fb2063` ended `failure`. 199 test binaries report `test result: FAILED` in the `gate-logs` artifact.

## Cause

PR #2293 (`e2ca9443b`) reads posts and machine files from disk at run time (`crates/post/src/data_dir.rs`). The dev candidates (`<profile>/../../assets`, `<manifest>/../../assets`) apply only when `cargo_profile_dir` finds the cargo build tree. It finds the tree only by the old cargo layout:

- the exe folder is `target/<profile>` or `target/<profile>/{deps,examples}`;
- that profile folder holds `.fingerprint`.

The cargo of the runner uses the new build-dir layout. Test executables are in `target/debug/build/<pkg>/<hash>/out/`, not in `target/debug/deps/`. Fingerprints are in each unit folder, so `target/debug/.fingerprint` does not exist. Thus `cargo_profile_dir` returns `None`, and the lookup tries only `<exe dir>/assets/<kind>`.

Evidence from the artifact logs:

```
     Running unittests src/lib.rs (target/debug/build/camcraft-post/4d4a6b2fbedf41a7/out/camcraft_post-4d4a6b2fbedf41a7)
thread 'data_dir::tests::the_dev_run_finds_the_repository_assets' panicked at crates/post/src/data_dir_tests.rs:123:52:
no posts folder found - the program needs its assets/posts directory beside the executable (looked in: /home/ghrunner/runner-work/Camcraft/Camcraft/target/debug/build/camcraft-post/4d4a6b2fbedf41a7/out/assets/posts)
```

Each "looked in" list in the logs has one path only (hash replaced by `H`, count of lines):

```
    424 .../target/debug/build/camcraft-app/H/out/assets/posts
    213 .../target/debug/build/camcraft-app/H/out/assets/machines
     15 .../target/debug/build/camcraft-ui/H/out/assets/machines
     11 .../target/debug/build/camcraft-ui/H/out/assets/posts
      4 .../target/debug/assets/posts          (camcraft-cli, the uplifted binary)
      1 .../target/debug/build/camcraft-post/H/out/assets/posts
```

The last-but-one line shows that the uplifted `target/debug/camcraft-cli` also fails. Thus `target/debug/.fingerprint` is absent in this layout, and a dev run (`cargo run`) with this cargo also fails.

Windows worktrees pass because the local cargo (1.99.0) uses the old layout.

## Grouped failures

1. Lookup (most binaries): the panic text or the refusal names `no posts folder found` or `no machines folder found`. Examples: `post` lib, `shipped_from_disk`, `logging`, `wcs_index`, `rigid_tapping`, `mcp_live`, `lathe_work_spindle`, `ui` lib, `ui` `machine`.
2. Lookup, shown as a different assertion: tests that compare against a shipped machine or post. Examples: `control_comp` and `wear_comp` goldens (the program has `(CAMCRAFT)` and no `M8`, because the default machine is not read), `lathe_workholding_live`, `ui` `machine_mode_tests` and `gate_route_tests`.
3. Not yet explained: `camcraft-motion` `corner_arc_radius` (`Waterline: no corner turned on an arc`). The motion crate does not read posts. The fix of this issue examines it on Windows and reports.

## Done means

- `cargo_profile_dir` accepts the old and the new cargo layout, for test executables and for the uplifted binaries.
- An installed exe without its `assets/<kind>` folder is still refused by name.
- A unit test pins the new layout and fails without the fix.
- The next post-merge run shows no `no posts folder found` and no `no machines folder found`.

What happens: a Deburr operation that takes the stock as its source cuts about 0.94 mm into a part, and the setup posts G-code. The part was there at generation. No refusal shows.

Expected: the post is refused, and the refusal names the operation and the part.

Evidence:

- The same result occurs on `main` at `3f41b8da6`. PR #2312 does not change it.
- Possible cause, from the review: the stock simulation gives the edge-break credit (#303) to the Deburr bevel. Thus the simulation finds no gouge. When the reviewer added `Deburr` to the match in `crates/app/src/stock_sim_breaks.rs:36` (a file of PR #2312), the simulation refused the post.
- A Deburr has no stock-source part law today. A Deburr on a stock made from the model can be a legal edge break. The fix must keep that case legal.

Found during the review of PR #2312 (issue #2308). The two defects have the same family: a stock-source edge operation gets a credit that hides a gouge.

Done means:
- A test pins that a stock-source Deburr that cuts into a part does not post, and that the refusal names the operation and the part. The test uses aligned stock and stock turned a quarter about Z.
- A test pins that a legal Deburr of a part edge still posts.

title: A stock-source 2D Chamfer into a part added after generation posts when the program sim judges the stock

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
A stock-source 2D Chamfer can post a cut into a part. This occurs when the part is added after generation and the program sim judges the stock.

## Reproduction

The fixture of `crates/app/tests/stock_source_holes.rs` (`stock_source_chamfer_refusal_names_cause_and_part_as_source_workaround`, the "chamfer-rejudge-hint" case):

1. Use `job(Model::hole(3.0, 8.0), HALF, rotated)` with `HALF = 35`.
2. Generate a stock-source 2D Chamfer, `chamfer(1.0)`. The generation is clean.
3. Import a part "other": a plate on x [30, 35], y [-5, 5], z [0, 20].
4. Call `posting::post_setup`.

Result on `main` at `7e26134bf`:

- Stock aligned: `POSTED`. The program has `G01 X35. Y-35. Z19.` along the edge of "other".
- Stock turned a quarter about Z: `POSTED` (the red case of #2306).
- Stock turned 1e-6 rad about Z (the sim does not judge): `post blocked - ... S1 now cuts part 'other' (move 5 cuts past the finish surface (stock-source chamfer breaks into a part; ...`.

## Cause

In `crates/app/src/posting_sim.rs`, `judge_clause` calls `kept_moved` (the live re-judge of #1628, `operation::kept_rejudge::moved_part_problem`) only in the `Err(reason)` arm, when the sim does not judge. In the `Ok(_)` arm with zero gouge cells, the re-judge does not run. The column sim does not see this chamfer cut into "other". Thus the post goes out.

- The aligned case exists since #1628 (commit `329db7d80`).
- #2182 (#2177) made the sim judge a quarter-turned box. Thus the quarter-turned case now also posts.

## Proposed fix

Run `kept_moved` also in the `Ok(_)` arm when the sim finds no gouge. Add a pinning test for the aligned and the quarter-turned stock. Then run each suite that posts, because the change can add refusals.

Found during #2306.

labels.name: bug

labels.name: P2

body:
Maintainer, 2026-11-16: "Issue, Bug, P2, mch, cps, themes, scripts - should be read from disk at runtme and not dompiled into the binary."

What happens: the build compiles these data files into the executable with `include_bytes!` / `include_str!`. Known places:

- the post processor scripts (`assets/posts/*.cps`), in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` (54 includes);
- the machine files (`.mch`);
- the themes;
- the scripts.

A user cannot change, add or replace one of these files without a new build. An executable without an `assets` directory beside it shows all of them.

Expected: the application reads these files from disk at run time.

Work:

- List each `include_bytes!` / `include_str!` of a machine file, a post script, a theme or a script in `crates/*/src`. Icons, the application icon and fonts are not in the scope of this issue.
- Define one data directory lookup (beside the executable first, then the per-user data directory) in one module. Each reader uses it.
- Read the files at start or on first use, and cache the result. Do not read a file per frame.
- A missing or malformed file gives a clear error that names the file and the directory. It does not crash. A post script that fails to load refuses the post by name.
- Each release package ships the directories (see PR #2044, which ships `examples`). Packaging script and workflow changes need the maintainer's decision: name them in the PR body.
- The browser build has no disk. Keep the compiled-in copy for the `wasm32` target only, and say so.
- Tests read the files from the repository `assets` directory.

Safety: a post script read from disk can be edited by a user, and it then changes the posted G-code. Show the path of the loaded post script in the post dialog or the program header comment, so that a user can see which file made the program. The verify check and the post gate do not change.

Open design questions (the worker records its choice in `docs/decisions/`):

- Whether a compiled-in copy stays as a fallback on desktop when the directory is missing. The maintainer's words say no.
- The order of the lookup when the same file name is in two directories.

Done means: the desktop executable holds no compiled-in machine file, post script, theme or script. A test pins that an edited file on disk changes what the application loads. A test pins the error for a missing directory. The packages of a cut hold the directories.

Reported by the maintainer in chat, 2026-11-16, with two screenshots (build `v0.22.0 · f6c7f605`, a local test build):

> "Bug in 2D Adapive. This was generated by setting a stock boundary and picking the outside edge of the part. I will helix down the first hole and clearing it out all the other Entrys inside and outside the part is missing lead ins of same helix setting. Same issue if i remove the boundary.. Only a helix leadin on the first pocket.. not the secondd one. This kinda comes back to how containment is getting interpreted... But problem ppeprsista even if i pick two inside faces of the pockets.. Helix is only on the first pocket, second is justa straight plunge into the material with no warning."

What happens:

- Project `testdata/models/fig8.camproj` (model `fig8.step`), 2D Adaptive, tool `EM-0800-4FL` (8 mm end mill), post Fanuc (built-in).
- Lead in / Lead out page: Entry Type `Helix`, Helix radius 1.6 mm, Minimum radius, pitch and angle on Auto, Plunge enabled.
- The operation generates: "8832 moves (27 plunge(s) @ 300, 3 level(s), 2286 arc(s)), 12 warning(s)".
- The first pocket gets the helix entry. Each other entry, inside and outside the part, is a straight plunge into the material.
- No warning names the plunges.
- The result is the same for three selections: stock boundary with the outside edge; no boundary; the two inside faces of the pockets.

Expected:

- Each entry into material uses the selected entry type (helix), at each region and each level.
- Where the helix does not fit, the ramp comes next. A straight plunge into material is the last fallback only.
- Each entry that falls back gets a warning that names the region, the level and the reason. The page says "where the helix cannot fit, a ramp and then a plunge stand in": the user must see when this happens.
- A plunge into material with a tool that cannot cut at its centre is refused or blocks the post, by the rule that the project has for such tools.
- A plunge in open air (outside the stock, or in an area that an earlier pass cleared) needs no helix and no warning.

To find:

1. Why the entry planner gives the helix to the first region only. Does it try the helix for each region, or one time for the operation?
2. If the 27 plunges are in material or in cleared area, by the stock state at that moment.
3. If the Offset rings fallback is the cause. The status line says "the HSM plan is refused: the area is a channel 10.6 mm wide ..."; the fallback path possibly does not apply the entry settings.
4. Why no warning is made.

Safety: a straight plunge into uncut material without a warning is wrong output that can break a tool. The fix changes posted G-code of 2D Adaptive (entry moves) and is under the safety floor. The verify check and the post gate do not become weaker. No real control run exists.

Related: #2232 (containment Outside, option 1 selected), and the "feed moves cross in XY at shared depth" warnings on this project (seen in the review of PR #2214).

Done means: a test on a part with two separate pockets (and one with an outside region) asserts a helix or ramp entry at each region and level where it fits, and a named warning for each entry that falls back to a plunge in material. The goldens that change are named in the PR.

5. A budget test: a frame without a change is below 10 ms on the reference models. The gate runs it.

body:
Found by the worker of #2210 (PR #2214); filed by an agent.

What happens: the UI helper `boundary_picks::extend_to_loop` reads face normals in the model frame. It does not apply the part alignment of the setup. For a turn about Z the result is the same. For a flip or a free angle, the helper can add a different face to the selection than the one that the user expects.

Expected: the helper reads the normals in the setup frame, with the same transform that the generators use for picks.

Effect: the helper fills in a selection only. It does not cut. The user sees the selected faces before a generate. A wrong pick is thus visible, but it can go into a boundary that the generator then obeys.

Evidence: PR #2214 body, "not exercised"; `docs/decisions/2210-aligned-area-controls.md`.

Done means: a test with a flipped setup (180 degrees about X) pins that `extend_to_loop` selects the same faces as in the same part with the flip built into its mesh.

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat on 2026-11-16, build v0.22.0 `ef1f5345`; filed by an agent. The maintainer set the priority:

> "Bug, P1; 2D Adaptive; generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: 2D Adaptive1: invalid machining parameters: setup 'Setup1' holds the part turned (part alignment) - area controls are not supported yet in an aligned setup"

## What happens

1. Open `testdata/models/fig8.camproj` (model `fig8.step`, vise fixture, stock, tool `EM-0800-4FL`, one 2D Adaptive). The files are in the maintainer's checkout (see #2209).
2. `Setup1` holds the part turned (part alignment).
3. The 2D Adaptive has an edge chain selection on the Geometry tab.
4. Click Generate.

Result: no toolpath. The message is:

```
generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: 2D Adaptive1: invalid machining parameters: setup 'Setup1' holds the part turned (part alignment) - area controls are not supported yet in an aligned setup
```

## Expected

A 2D Adaptive generates in an aligned setup, with its area selection. A part that is turned onto the vise is a usual setup, and a 2D Adaptive is the usual first roughing operation.

## Facts for the fix

- The refusal is deliberate ("not supported yet"). It is not a crash and it does not give a wrong toolpath. The work is to supply the missing behaviour, not to remove the guard.
- The area controls (the picked chain or face, the boundary) must go through the part alignment transform into the setup frame, with the same transform that the model and the stock use.
- Find each operation that has the same refusal (search for the message text) and list them on this issue. Fix them with one shared transform, or file one issue for the others.
- The message does not tell the user what to do. If a case stays refused, the message names the control to clear.

## Safety

The fix is under the safety floor: it changes where the tool cuts in an aligned setup. A wrong transform (sign, order or pivot) cuts in the wrong place.

- Pin with a setup where the part is turned 90 degrees and the area is not symmetric, so that a wrong frame gives a different region.
- The verify check and the post gate judge the result against the turned part and the stock.
- Do not remove the refusal before the transform has its tests.

Done means: `fig8.camproj` generates its 2D Adaptive in the aligned setup; a test pins the cut region against the turned part; each other operation with this refusal is fixed or has its own issue.

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat on 2026-11-16, build v0.22.0 `ef1f5345`; filed by an agent:

> "the model imported (fig8.step in testdata) - has chamfer so the edge below the chamfer look like this ... an enormous amount of small sections rather than a welded edge like the one above."

## What happens

1. Import `fig8.step`. The model has a swept (figure-eight) wall with a chamfer at its top.
2. Add a 2D Adaptive. On the Geometry tab set "Click selects" to Edges.
3. Click the upper edge of the chamfer. The pick is one edge: `Chain fig8 · open · 113.1 mm · 1 of 1`.
4. Click the edge below the chamfer (chamfer to wall). Each click picks a piece of about 0.9 mm. Four Ctrl+clicks give `Chain fig8 · open · 0.9 mm · 1 of 4` to `4 of 4`.

## Expected

The edge below the chamfer is one feature edge, as the edge above it is. One click picks its full length. A chain made from it has one row.

## Why it matters

- The user cannot select this edge for a 2D operation in practice: an edge of about 113 mm needs more than 100 clicks.
- A chain of many short open pieces can give a toolpath with many short moves, or a refusal, where one smooth chain is correct.
- The rule of #692 says that only feature edges are pickable, never tessellation edges. These pieces look like tessellation or patch joints that the pick shows as feature edges.

## Where to look

- Find if the STEP file has this edge as many short edges (a chamfer made of many small faces), or if the kernel import or `decompose` splits one curve.
- If the file has many short edges that are tangent-continuous: join them to one pickable feature edge at import or at the pick (G1 chain below an angle limit).
- If the import splits one curve: keep the curve as one edge.
- Compare with the upper chamfer edge of the same model, which is one edge.

Workaround: Shift+click picks the whole loop, where the loop is the wanted geometry.

Safety floor: the change is in model geometry or its edge topology, which feeds chains and toolpaths. Thus `effort:high`.

Related: #692 (feature edges only), #1505 (edge picking), #2201 (slow frames while an edge is selected, same model and session).

Done means: on `fig8.step`, one click on the edge below the chamfer picks the full edge as one chain row, and a test on that file pins the edge count of the chamfer's lower boundary.

body:
Found while working #1749 (the user's `sc_logo.camproj`). Related to #2180 (a band that only touches the shank top). This case is wider: the holder band starts below the stated shank top, beside the shank.

## What happens

The tool T31 has `shank_d` 6.35 (the same as the cutter). Its drawn holder body starts 38.1 mm above the tip. The stated shank top is 65.278 mm. So the holder band stands beside the shank from 38.1 to 65.278 mm.

`tool_body::judged` calls `HolderProfile::enclose` (`crates/tools/src/holder_profile.rs`). `enclose` widens the whole judged shank, from the flute top (14.478 mm) upward, to the band diameter (35 mm).

Results on the user's project (forced regeneration, main `ce59ef446`):
- The #1844 reach preflight refuses "S1 Notch adaptive + terrace finish". The refusal is false.
- `verify` reports false `shank_hit` findings on four ops: 8138, 6884, 479 and 219 findings. They hold the post.

## Expected

The judged body follows the drawn tool: the shank stays Ø6.35 below the holder foot. The holder band counts only where it is (from 38.1 mm up). A real holder collision must still be found and must still hold the post.

## Why it matters

The refusal is safe, but it is wrong. The user cannot post a legal program. This blocks `sc_logo.camproj` from a clean post, whatever happens with #1749.

## Safety

Do not make the judged body smaller than the real tool anywhere. Pin both directions:
- the false refusal goes away for a holder above the reach;
- a holder band that does reach the stock still gives `shank_hit` / holder findings and holds the post.

Done means: on a fixture like T31 (shank Ø6.35, holder from 38.1 mm, shank top 65.278 mm), the reach preflight and verify judge the shank at Ø6.35 below 38.1 mm; a test with a holder that touches the stock still refuses; #2180's case is checked too.

title: 2D Contour with an exit point past a rounded corner is refused at the post: the overlap re-cuts the corner arc as chords and the crossing law convicts it

labels.name: bug

body:
## What happens

A closed 2D Contour with an exit point (#1473) whose overlap runs past a rounded corner generates `ok`, but `verify` blocks it with crossing findings and the post is refused:

```
post: post blocked - 18 warning(s): C1: feed moves 5 and 15 cross in XY at shared depth; C1: feed moves 5 and 17 cross in XY at shared depth; ...
```

## Reproduction (main 4b7a6b1e, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

The part is a 60 × 40 × 10 plate (z 0 to 10) with a 30 × 20 × 5 pocket, as a closed, outward-wound ASCII STL. The outside contour runs at offset 3 with r 3 arcs at the four corners.

```json
[["load_machine", {"builtin": "VMC 3-axis"}],
 ["import_model", {"path": "plate2.stl"}],
 ["set_stock", {"box": {"dx": 70, "dy": 50, "dz": 10}}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "EM-0600-4FL"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "contour", "tool": "EM-0600-4FL", "name": "C1", "source": "plate2",
   "params": {"top_z": {"offset": 0, "reference": "top_of_model"}, "bottom_z": {"offset": -3, "reference": "top_of_model"}, "stepdown": 3,
              "links": {"approach": {"start_point": [30, 0], "exit_point": [0, -20]}}}}],
 ["generate", {"name": "C1"}], ["verify", {}], ["post", {"output": "c1.nc"}]]
```

The moves of the first level, read from the cached toolpath in a throwaway test:

```
  3 Feed (33,8) -> (33,0)                     lead-in to the start point
  4 Feed (33,0) -> (33,-20)
  5 Feed (33,-20) -> (30,-23)  arc c=(30,-20)  first lap: the corner as one arc
  ... the whole ring ...
 12 Feed (33,20) -> (33,0)
 13 Feed (33,0) -> (33,-20)                   overlap toward the exit
 14-27 Feed (33,-20) -> ... -> (30,-23)       the same corner again, as 14 straight chords
 28 Feed (30,-23) -> (0,-23)                  to the exit point's projection
 29 Feed (0,-23) -> (-8,-23)                  lead-out
```

The chords of moves 14–27 lie inside move 5's arc, and the crossing law reads each as crossing it at the same depth.

## Neighbour cases that work (same document)

| Contour | `verify` | Post |
|---|---|---|
| no start or exit point | clean | 67 lines |
| `start_point` [30, 0] only | clean | 67 lines |
| `start_point` [30, 0], `exit_point` [30, −10] (overlap stays on the straight right wall) | clean | 69 lines |
| `start_point` [30, 0], `exit_point` [0, −20] (overlap passes the corner arc) | 18 crossings | refused |

## Root cause (likely)

`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_start.rs` says it for #1473: "the ring is cut all the way round, then on along its own polyline to the pick's projection". The first lap reaches the post arc-fitted (move 5 is one arc). The overlap is the ring's raw polyline (the 14 chords). Verify law (a) (`crossing`) then sees chord against arc at shared depth.

An overlap on straight segments only, which repeats exact segments, is not flagged. This is read from the moves above; the fitting call was not traced.

## Expected

The overlap to an exit point re-cuts the ring along the same moves the first lap used (the same arcs), so the program verifies and posts like the start-point-only contour. The overlap must not be refused for re-tracing its own wall.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P3`: a legal program refused. Putting the exit on the start's own edge works around it.
- `effort:high`
- `area:2d`
- `source:agent`

Related: #1473 (start and exit points), #1448.

title: useRadiusArcs posts helix half-turns whose R cannot reach the end point (chord 2.469 > 2R 2.468): R and end points are rounded separately, near-180 arcs are not split

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

With the script option `useRadiusArcs: true` (#258), the Fanuc post writes the helix entry's half-turns as R arcs that no circle of the written radius can draw. The chord between the posted end points is longer than 2R:

```
G03 X2.501 Y-0.493 Z11. R1.235 F1200
G03 X0.032 Y-0.493 Z10. R1.234 F1200      <- from (2.501, -0.493): chord 2.469, 2R = 2.468
```

The two half-turns of one helix also get two different radii, R1.235 and R1.234.

## Reproduction (main 4b7a6b1e, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

The part is a 60 × 40 × 10 plate with a Ø25, 5 mm deep round pocket: a closed, outward-wound ASCII STL with 96-segment walls. The pocket floor face is picked; Bottom Z is `bottom_of_selection`. The document's post is the default Fanuc. Post without a `post` name, because #2190 drops script options when one is named.

```json
[["load_machine", {"builtin": "VMC 3-axis"}],
 ["import_model", {"path": "round.stl"}],
 ["set_stock", {"box": {"dx": 60, "dy": 40, "dz": 10}}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "EM-0600-4FL"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "pocket", "tool": "EM-0600-4FL", "name": "PW", "source": "round", "params": {"strategy": "waterline", "stepdown": 5}}],
 ["set_operation_geometry", {"operation": "PW", "picks": [{"model": "round", "id": "<pocket floor face>"}]}],
 ["edit_operation", {"name": "PW", "params": {"bottom_z": {"offset": 0, "reference": "bottom_of_selection"}, "helix_radius": 1.2344}}],
 ["generate", {"name": "PW"}], ["verify", {}],
 ["set_post_options", {"script_options": {"useRadiusArcs": true}}],
 ["post", {"output": "r.nc"}]]
```

`verify` is clean and the post succeeds. Four of the helix half-turns have chord − 2|R| = +0.001 mm: arcs whose end point the radius cannot reach.

## Neighbour case that works

The same job with the seeded `helix_radius` of 1.2 (0.4 × the 6 mm tool's radius) posts R1.2 half-turns whose chord is exactly 2.400 = 2R. Across its 32 arcs, none has a chord over 2|R| and none sweeps more than 180°. With `useRadiusArcs` off, the 1.2344 helix posts as I/J.

## Root cause (confirmed)

`emitArcWithRadius` in `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` writes `R` as the unrounded distance from the start point to the centre. It writes X/Y as the end point, each rounded separately to three decimals. It splits only an exact full circle (`< 1e-5`). An arc at or near 180°, which every helix half-turn is, keeps a chord equal to 2R before rounding. Rounding the end points and R separately can then put the chord over 2R, as above.

The same function, with the same full-circle-only split, is in `haas.cps`, `mazak.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`, `tormach.cps` and `grblhal.cps` (they were not run here).

## Expected

R-form output never posts an arc whose R cannot reach its end point. For example, arcs at or near 180° stay in I/J or are split, as the exact full circle already is. The written R and end points then agree after rounding.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P1`: wrong posted G-code, but only with `useRadiusArcs` on (off by default).
- `effort:high`
- `area:post`
- `source:agent`

body:
## What happens

Per-post script options stored with `set_post_options { "script_options": ... }` (#258) are dropped without a word when the MCP `post` tool is given a `post` name. That includes naming the post the document already uses. The same document posted without a `post` name applies them.

## Reproduction (main 4b7a6b1e, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

```json
[["load_machine", {"builtin": "VMC 3-axis"}],
 ["set_stock", {"box": {"dx": 60, "dy": 40, "dz": 10}}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "EM-1000-4FL"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "face", "tool": "EM-1000-4FL", "name": "F1"}],
 ["generate", {}],
 ["set_post_options", {"script_options": {"showSequenceNumbers": "every-block", "writeToolList": true, "safeRetract": "G53"}}],
 ["post", {"output": "named.nc", "post": "Fanuc"}],
 ["post", {"output": "doc.nc"}]]
```

`set_post_options` answers with `"post": "Fanuc (built-in)"` and the three options set. Both posts succeed with no warning.

`doc.nc` (no `post` named) has them:

```
O0001 (VMC 3-AXIS)
(T1 - FLAT END MILL D10. EM-1000-4FL)
N10 G21
...
N340 G53 G00 Z0.
N350 M30
```

`named.nc` (`"post": "Fanuc"`) has none of them: no N words, no tool list, and the default `G28` retract instead of the chosen `G53`.

The same happens with `useRadiusArcs: true` on a round waterline pocket. `"post": "Fanuc"` writes every arc with I/J, byte-identical to the option off.

## Root cause (confirmed)

`posting::program_options_for_script` merges the stored options only when it is given the post:

```rust
let mut overrides = post
    .map(|p| crate::setup_post_options::script_for_post(world, setup, p))
    .unwrap_or_default();
```

The MCP `post` tool calls `script::api::v_post`. With a `cps` given, that goes through `posting_mounts::post_mounts_script_with_options` → `posting::post_script_with_script_options`, which calls `post_script_as(..., None, None, extra)`. With `post: None` the stored options are never read. Only `extra` would apply: `v_post`'s `options` key, which the MCP `post` tool does not expose.

## Expected

When the named post is one the stored options belong to (here, the document's own Fanuc), those options apply, as they do with no name given. Otherwise the post says it did not apply them; it must not drop the user's `safeRetract` or arc form unseen.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P3`: a set option that silently does nothing on one path.
- `effort:medium`
- `area:post`
- `area:mcp`
- `source:agent`


`verify` is clean. `post` returns one file, `perop.nc`, 115 lines, with the excerpt above at the S1 → S2 change.

Same document, same `post` call, only the option differs:

| Option | Output at the S1 → S2 change |
|---|---|

| `per_op: true` | no stop, and one combined file |

In the GUI, Output "One file per operation" writes "each operation as its own standalone program into a folder" (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/pages.rs`, #111). The browser build refuses that post outright (`browser_files::refusal`, `NO_FOLDER`). Neither GUI path writes this combined program.

## Root cause (confirmed)

- `stop_of` in `crates/app/src/posting_setup_change.rs` returns no stop whenever `per_op` is set ("run straight on, one file per setup, or one file per operation"). The stop is dropped in the stream, before any post script runs, so every post is affected.

So `per_op` removes the stop that only per-operation files make safe, and this path then writes the operations into one file anyway. The same holds for a script's `cam.post`.

The MCP `post` (and `cam.post`) with `per_op` on writes one file per operation, as the GUI does, or refuses by name. It must never write a combined program whose setup change has lost its stop.

body:
## What happens

On a model whose shell `pick::align::outward_normal` cannot judge, `list_features` still prints a definite `facing` and `normal` for each face. These are the sign-canonical plane normal, so a bottom face reads `"facing": "up"`. Opposite walls share one normal. Nothing in the row says the outside was not known.

`lay_part_on_face` on the same face refuses, naming the reason:

```
list_features:    face:0x38c06ba55fa364b3  "facing": "up", "normal": [0.0, 0.0, 1.0]   bounds z 0.0 .. 0.0  (the bottom)
lay_part_on_face: face 0x38c06ba55fa364b3 of 'plate' belongs to an open body (its shell has holes), so its outside cannot be told - repair the mesh (fill its holes) or align to a closed part
```

This is the case #884 and #956 named: an agent picks faces by `facing` and `normal` for `locate_part`, `set_wcs_from_features` and operation geometry.

## Reproduction (main 4b7a6b1e, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

The part is a 60 × 40 × 10 plate (z 0 to 10) with a 30 × 20 pocket, 5 deep, written as ASCII STL with outward winding (28 facets). Its top face is written as four rectangles around the pocket opening, so their long edges meet the pocket's top edges in T-junctions. Every facet is wound outward. For example, the bottom face's facets have normal −Z.

```json
[["import_model", {"path": "plate.stl"}],
 ["list_features", {"model": "plate"}],
 ["add_setup", {}],
 ["lay_part_on_face", {"face": {"model": "plate", "id": "face:0x38c06ba55fa364b3"}}]]
```

`list_features` faces, as printed:

| Face (bounds) | `facing` | `normal` |
|---|---|---|
| bottom, z 0 | `up` | `[0, 0, 1]` |
| wall y = −20 | `side` | `[0, 1, 0]` |
| wall y = +20 | `side` | `[0, 1, 0]` |
| wall x = −30 | `side` | `[1, 0, 0]` |
| wall x = +30 | `side` | `[1, 0, 0]` |
| pocket wall y = −10 | `side` | `[0, 1, 0]` |
| pocket wall y = +10 | `side` | `[0, 1, 0]` |

`lay_part_on_face` refuses as quoted above.

## Neighbour case that works

The same plate with its top ring written as four trapezoids, so every edge is shared by exactly two facets, is a closed shell. `list_features` gives the bottom `"down"` `[0, 0, -1]`, the walls their outward normals (`[0, -1, 0]` / `[0, 1, 0]`, `[-1, 0, 0]` / `[1, 0, 0]`), and the pocket walls pointing into the pocket. `lay_part_on_face` on its bottom succeeds ("Flip over X", outside −Z).

## Root cause (confirmed)

`outward()` in `crates/app/src/mcp/features.rs` calls `outward_normal` and, when it refuses, falls back to `world_dir(loc, fa.normal)`, the canonical normal. Its comment: "Where it refuses (an open or inside-out shell, no usable plane) the row keeps the canonical normal, placed - a listing must not fail on one face". `facing()` then makes "up" / "down" / "side" from whichever normal it got.

#956's "Done means" asked for the outward normal "or a refusal-shaped field when the winding is not decidable". The shipped fix (PR #1046) took the first half only.

The `camcraft-mcp` skill still carries #937's caveat in the `set_wcs_from_features` row: "a `list_features` face row's `normal` is the plane's canonical normal, not its outward side - tell faces apart by `bounds`". #956 asked for that note to be removed. As it stands, it is wrong for closed shells and is the only warning for open ones.

## Expected

The listing must not fail on one face, and it must not guess either. A face whose outside cannot be told says so in its row: for example, `facing` and `normal` null, or a flag with `outward_normal`'s reason. The skill note then describes that field instead of the old caveat.

- `P3`: a misleading field on the agent surface. The tools that act on a face refuse correctly.

## 1. A Tool axis A of 180 is refused, and the refusal gives no reason

Steps:
1. Mount `Tormach 770MX + microARC 4`. Add a tool and a box stock.
2. Add a Slot. On the Heights tab, tick **Tilted plane (3+2)**. Set **Tool axis A** to 180 and **Tool axis B** to 0. Choose **Apply**.

Result: the edit is refused with this text: `operation parameters are not usable for a Slot operation`. The MCP tool gives the same text: `add_operation: invalid parameters: operation parameters are not usable for a Slot operation`.

The cause is `Tilt::is_sane` in `crates/app/src/operation/types/params.rs`. It accepts A from -90 to 90 and B from -180 to 180. The pose law writes the face opposite the top as A 0, B 180. The refusal does not name the tilt, the limits, or the A 0 B 180 pose. A microARC 4 user thinks in A only, and cannot find the remedy from this text.

The workaround is to type A 0 and B 180. The guide page for #1904 documents it.

## 2. The plane of the A 0 B 180 face has X and Y exchanged

`TiltedFrame::new` (`crates/cl/src/cl/frame.rs`) selects the in-plane axes from the smallest component of the tool axis. For A 90 and A -90, plane X is machine X (the rotary axis). For A 0 B 180, `sin(180 degrees)` is not exactly zero, the seed becomes Y, and plane X is machine Y and plane Y is machine X.

Result: the same flat along the bar has the ends (-0.75, 0) and (-0.25, 0) on three faces, but (0, -0.75) and (0, -0.25) on the fourth face. The page does not show the plane axes, so the user finds this only from the toolpath preview.

The posted program is correct in each case. The post reads the tool tip in machine coordinates.

## Proposed change

- Refuse an out-of-range tilt by name. Give the limits, and say that the face opposite the top is A 0 B 180.
- Or accept A beyond 90 degrees at the door and store the canonical pose.
- For a pose with no X component of the tool axis, keep plane X on machine X. Or show the plane X and Y directions on the page.

A change to the frame basis changes the paths of existing A 0 B 180 operations. Thus this work is under the safety floor.

Done means: a user who types Tool axis A = 180 on an A-table machine gets the A180 index or a refusal that names the remedy. The plane X of the A 0 B 180 face is on the rotary axis, or the page shows the plane axes. A test pins each item. The guide page `first-4axis-part.md` is updated.

Refs #1904, #797.

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-15, on v0.21.0, with a screenshot of a 2D Adaptive operation.

His words: "a common issue i see is that the first toolpath is always ontop of the part at TopZ ... even thos stepdown states "full depth" of the cut.. technically it should just be one single toolpath right?" and "find it in all operations.. This is a high effortf, P2 bug.."

## What happens

The operation has Top Z = 13 (stock top + 1), Bottom Z = 0 and Stepdown = 50 mm. It posts two full levels: one at Z 13 and one at Z 0. The level at Top Z cuts no material. It doubles the cycle time of a one-level cut.

## Cause

The shared level law starts its list at Top Z:

```rust
// crates/motion/src/machining2d/levels.rs, cut_levels
let mut z = top;
while z > bottom + tol {
    zs.push(z);      // the first level is `top`
    z -= stepdown;
}
zs.push(bottom);
```

`cut_levels(13, 0, 50)` gives `[13, 0]`. The correct list is `[0]`. With a stepdown of 5 it gives `[13, 8, 3, 0]`. The correct list is `[8, 3, 0]`.

`crates/app/src/operation/area.rs` `ladder_planes` restates the same law, and its unit test pins the wrong list (`ladder_planes(20.0, 0.0, 5.0) == [20, 15, 10, 5, 0]`).

## Callers found (read-only search, not complete)

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/`: `adaptive_troch.rs:158`, `bore.rs:308`, `circular.rs:278` and `:280`, `contour_params.rs:216` (2D Contour), `face.rs:156`, `pocket.rs:277`, `pocket_hsm.rs:49` and `pocket_troch.rs:68` (level counts for the budget), `slots.rs:160` and `:343`, `trochoid_slot.rs:319`
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/entry.rs:89`, `:123`, `:236`, `:258` (3D Pocket and its rest pass)
- `crates/app/src/operation/area.rs:74`, `:182`, `:233` (`ladder_planes`, the 3D pocket region build)
- `crates/motion/tests/control_comp.rs` (a test helper with the same name)

Not yet read: `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/ladder.rs` `levels`, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_depth.rs` `ladder`, `crates/motion/src/machining3d/ladder.rs`, the turning, drilling (peck), engraving, chamfer, plasma and EDM depth ladders, and each operation with its own loop.

## For the work

1. Audit each operation of each machine type for a level at Top Z (or at the material top) that removes no material. List each in the PR with the result.
2. Fix the shared law so that the first level is `top - stepdown`, and the last level is `bottom` exactly. Use one law: `ladder_planes` in `app` must use the motion law, or match it by a shared test.
3. Check the special cases:
   - Top Z below the stock top (material above Top Z): no level may cut more than one stepdown. Find what each operation means by Top Z, and state it.
   - `circular.rs:278` starts at a previous level (`cut_levels(prev, floor, ...)`): make sure that it does not cut the previous level two times.
   - Face: a single pass at `cut_z` stays one pass.
   - A stepdown of 0 or a span of 0: the current refusal and the one-plane result stay.
   - Rest machining and the 3D Pocket shell levels: the level count and the budget readings change. Restate the budget pins with the reason.
   - The ramp, helix and plunge entries that read `top_z` as the material top (`Motion::top_z`) must stay correct.
4. The size of the last step (the remainder or equal steps) is a separate choice. Keep the current remainder rule, and file a follow-up issue for the choice.

This changes posted G-code for existing projects (one level fewer for each depth-stepping operation). It is under the safety floor.

## Done means

- No operation posts a level at Top Z that removes no material when Top Z is at or above the material top.
- One-level case: Top Z 13, Bottom Z 0, Stepdown 50 gives one level at Z 0. Pinned for 2D Adaptive, 2D Pocket, 2D Contour, Slot, Bore, Circular and 3D Pocket.

body:
Design 5-axis kinematics and Haas NGC multi-axis posting for trunnion tables (`TR160`, `TR210`, `TRT100`) and universal machining centers (`UMC-500`).

Public Haas specifications and codebase behavior expose these open problems:
- **Kinematics mismatch in CamCraft:** `crates/cl/src/cl/pose.rs:53` (`axis_to_angles`) outputs `[A, B, 0.0]` with `C` always zero, and `crates/app/src/machine/judge.rs:79-105` checks literal rotary letters without inverse kinematics. A `UMC-500` uses `B` (+120° to -35°) plus `C` (360°), which fails when any Y-tilted pose requests `A`. A `TR160`/`TRT100` calls its cradle `A` (±120°) and platter `B` (360°), where platter `B` turns perpendicular to tilted `A` rather than around static Y.
- **NGC 5-axis G-codes and options:** Haas NGC uses `G254`/`G255` (Dynamic Work Offset) for 3+2 indexing and `G234` (Tool Center Point Control, not Fanuc `G43.4`) for simultaneous 4/5-axis cutting. Both `G254` and `G234` are paid options (`haascnc.com`); controls without TCPC require `G93` inverse-time feed (`F = 1 / minutes` per move).
- **Brakes and limits:** 4th-axis (`M10`/`M11`) and 5th-axis (`M12`/`M13`) brakes clamp during indexed cuts and stay released (`M11`/`M13`) during simultaneous motion.

Deliver a design decision in `docs/decisions/` covering:
1. Inverse kinematics or kinematic-chain representation in `cl`/`judge.rs` for `B+C` UMCs and `A+B` trunnions (`TR160`/`TRT100`).
2. Option-gating rules in `.mch` and `haas.cps` for `G254`/`G255` (DWO), `G234` (TCPC), `G93` fallback, and `M10`–`M13` brakes.
3. Concrete implementation sub-issues for machine definitions, IK checks, and `haas.cps` 5-axis output.

Done means: A design decision in `docs/decisions/` defines the kinematic model, option gating, and implementation split for Haas 5-axis support.

- Keep `G93` `F` independent of `G20` (inch) vs `G21` (mm).

## Goal

- Take normalized 2D primitives (`Line`, `Arc`, `Circle`, `Polyline`) and layer names from #1860 together with a configurable join tolerance in millimeters (default `0.01` mm).

- Resolve closed chain nesting into outer boundaries vs inner holes using `geo2d::Region` / `clipper2-rust` winding rules.
- Reject self-crossing closed loops and degenerate chains with clear named errors instead of panicking.
- Handle T-junctions or branching vertices cleanly with deterministic traversal or named diagnostics.

## Done means
Tests chain unordered lines, arcs, and circles into stable `ChainId` loops and open chains within a specified tolerance; gaps wider than tolerance remain explicitly open; nested rectangles and circles classify accurately as outer loops vs holes; self-crossing loops return a named error; arc metadata survives chaining.

body:
Found while fixing #1604.

**What happens:** the post stream states the stock only as its axis-aligned box (`StockXYLeft/Right/Front/Back`, `StockZTop`). The fix for #1604 in `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps` uses the largest half-width of that box as the stock's radius about the spindle axis. That is exact for a round bar. **Workaround:** use a round-bar (cylinder) stock for lathe setups.

**Done means:** a lathe stream states the stock's turning radius; the Tormach lathe post's G30 approach and departure use it; a pin with a square-bar stock shows no G30-adjacent rapid inside the corners' circle.

title: post-merge.yml: the report job is skipped when the gate fails, so a red main opens no issue

labels.name: bug

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:low

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
What happens: post-merge run 43535610115 (push to main at 745edc36a) ended with job `gate` = failure and job `report` = skipped. The rolling issue `main is red (post-merge gate)` was not opened or commented on.

Expected: AGENTS.md "Fixes are tested in the background": a red post-merge gate opens or comments on the rolling issue; the next green run closes it.

Cause (read from `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml` on main): the `report` job has `needs: gate` and an `if:` with no status-check function:

```
if: ${{ (needs.gate.result == 'success' || needs.gate.result == 'failure') && needs.gate.outputs.skipped != 'true' && (...) }}
```

GitHub Actions adds an implicit `success()` to a job's `if` unless it contains `always()`, `failure()`, `cancelled()` or `!cancelled()`. With a failed `needs` job the implicit `success()` is false, so the job is skipped before the expression is read. The job therefore only ever runs on green.

Suggested fix: start the condition with `always() &&` (the rest already excludes cancelled and skipped runs). One line.

Note on this particular run: its only red test was `a_lowered_cap_refuses_the_same_face_at_once` (`crates/app/tests/import_step_guard.rs`, "not within 30s"), the wall-clock flake of issue 1605, so main was not truly red here. The reporting gap is real for any failure.

A `.github/` change: the PR is read, not built, and waits for the maintainer (`needs-maintainer`). `Process change: yes` does not apply (`.github/` is not a process file).

Found by the maintenance session while watching runs.

Done means: a post-merge run whose gate fails runs `report` and opens or comments on the rolling issue; a green run after it closes that issue; a cancelled or cut-skipped run still reports nothing.

Follow-up to #1315 (PR #1485), tested on macOS 27 (Apple silicon) with `/bin/bash` 3.2 and BSD sed at `0b4052bb`.

**What happens:** after #1485, the script gets through the sysroot download, the `shasum` check and the `sed` patching on macOS. With none found, it stops with a message naming what to install (`brew install llvm` or `rustup component add llvm-tools`) instead of failing at the link. "Needs:" in the header gains `llvm-ar` on macOS.

title: 2D ops cannot start below the material top: the entry rapids into uncut stock, so the air pass at Top cannot be avoided

body:
Found while programming a simple 2.5D end-cap plate (user's project) with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP. Re-checked on upstream main **d00243a5**: **still reproduces, identical output**.

## What happens

Every 2D depth ladder cuts its first level at `top_z` (#514, kept by the maintainer on 2026-11-11). When Top is the faced material top, that level is a full pass in air. The obvious way to avoid it, setting Top to the first real cut, is **refused**: the entry rapids straight down to Top + the plunge height, which is inside the uncut stock above Top, and verify convicts it:

`rapid move 1 travels below the clearance plane inside stock`

So the air pass cannot be avoided. In the user's project the bore adaptive (2D Adaptive, three 0.25 in levels) keeps an air level at the faced top: **about 5.6 of its 16.9 min**.

Repro (main and v0.19.0 alike), a plate in stock 0.5 mm taller, faced to the part top first, `stepdown: 4`, bottom at the part bottom:

| op | `top_z` | levels (z) | first moves | verify |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2D Adaptive (bore) | TOS -0.5 (faced top) | 10 (air), 6, 2, 0 | rapid to z 12, feed down | ok |
| 2D Adaptive (bore) | TOS -4.5 | 6, 2, 0 | **rapid to z 8** (stock is at z 10) | `rapid move 1 travels below the clearance plane inside stock` |
| 2D Contour inside (bore) | TOS -0.5 | 10 (air), 6, 2, 0 | rapid to z 12, plunge | ok |
| 2D Contour inside (bore) | TOS -4.5 | 6, 2, 0 | **rapid to z 8** | same message, moves 1 and 5 |

The rapid law is right to convict a rapid into stock; the generator is what puts it there.

## Minimal repro (MCP)

`plate_bore.stl`: a 100 x 60 x 10 mm plate, centred, z 0..10, with a centred Ø40 through bore.

```
import_model   {"path": "plate_bore.stl", "name": "plate"}
add_setup      {"name": "Setup 1"}
set_stock      {"box": {"dx": 110, "dy": 70, "dz": 10.5}}
set_wcs        {"stock_point": {"x": "center", "y": "center", "z": "max"}}
add_tool       {"catalog": "EM-0600-4FL", "name": "EM6"}
add_operation  {"kind": "Face", "tool": "EM6", "name": "face", "params": {"cut_z": {"reference": "top_of_stock", "offset": -0.5}}}
add_operation  {"kind": "2D Adaptive", "tool": "EM6", "name": "op", "source": "plate",
                "params": {"top_z": {"reference": "top_of_stock", "offset": -4.5},
                           "bottom_z": {"reference": "top_of_stock", "offset": -10.5}, "stepdown": 4}}
set_operation_geometry {"operation": "op", "picks": [the bore's top chain]}
generate {} ; verify {}  -> "rapid move 1 travels below the clearance plane inside stock"
```

## Expected

An op whose Top is below the material standing over it enters safely: it rapids to the plunge height above the **material actually there** (the prior stock, or the stock top), then feeds (helix, ramp or plunge) down to its first level. Then a user can set Top to the first real cut and skip the air pass, without reopening the #514 ladder decision.

## Done means

- The repro above (Adaptive and Contour, Top 4 mm below the faced top) generates an entry that rapids no lower than the plunge height above the remaining material and feeds the rest; verify is clean; pinned by a test for each.
- The rapid law (#96, #1066, #1091 pins) is unchanged.

Related: #514 (the air level at Top, won't-do for now), #1066.

`detect_holes` reports a through hole with `"floor_z"` at the part bottom and `"through": true`. - The 1.0 mm is not a parameter. It is not shown on the op, in the hole list or in `get_job`, and cannot be changed (the only way is to set `through: false` and type a deeper floor by hand, which is what the user did).
- It is not tied to anything under the part: not the stock bottom, a HAT web, the parallels or the setup. In the repro the part bottom is z 4.826 and the path goes to z 3.826 (the stock bottom is z 0). With the part bottom on the stock bottom, it cuts 1 mm below the stock, into whatever the part sits on, with no note (the fixture laws may catch a modelled parallel; an unmodelled table or spoilboard is not judged).
- It is in mm whatever the document units (an inch user would choose 0.020-0.040 in, and might want it scaled to the tool's tip, e.g. a drill's point length).

## Minimal repro (MCP)

```
import_model   {"path": "End Caps-End capSupport Plate.step", "name": "part"}
move_model     {"name": "part", "position": [0, 37.9, 4.826]}
add_setup      {"name": "Setup 1"}
set_stock      {"box": {"dx": 110, "dy": 185, "dz": 15.33}}
set_wcs        {"stock_point": {"x": "center", "y": "center", "z": "max"}}
add_tool       {"catalog": "EM-0400-2FL", "name": "EM4"}
add_operation  {"kind": "Bore", "tool": "EM4", "name": "Bore", "source": "part", "params": {"stepdown": 2.0}}
detect_holes   {"name": "Bore"}   -> every hole "floor_z": 4.826, "through": true
generate {}                       -> deepest feed z 3.826, no note
```

## Expected

- The break-through is a visible, editable op parameter (default 1.0 mm or a tool-relative value), in document units, saved with the project and settable over MCP.
- The op says what it did (a note: "through holes run 1.0 mm past the part bottom, to z ...").
- The depth past the part is checked against what is under it: never below the stock bottom unless the user allows it, and refused by name if it would reach a fixture.

## Done means

- A through-hole break-through parameter on Drill, Bore and Thread (GUI field, project file, MCP `params`), with a default equal to today's 1.0 mm so existing goldens hold.
- The generated note states the break-through depth; a through hole whose break-through would go below the stock bottom is noted or refused; pinned by tests.

Related: #1556 (large bores in hole detection).

Part of #1446 (first slice: the motion-crate generator, `camcraft_motion::machining2d::rest_plan` / `rest_pocket`, on branch `issue/1446-rest-2d`).

Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, quoted on #1446): "We wanna cover some of the toolpaths and things like that at first." and "Lets create issues on your suggestions, they made sense." Sources as he asked: "We should use perplexity to find literature on those types of toolpaths and not copy them straight up".

What the first slice leaves out of the generator, each of which needs design before code:

1. **2D Adaptive over a rest area.** `rest_pocket` refuses the Adaptive strategy by name. The adaptive plan picks its own entry and bounds engagement assuming a full pocket; over a rest area the entry should stand in cleared floor and the engagement model must know what is already cut.
2. **Entry from already-cut space.** The first slice plunges into each rest area like a plain pocket, so nothing depends on the cleared-area estimate. Entering sideways from cleared floor is faster, and makes that estimate safety-critical: the cleared area must be read small (it is today) and the entry refused, by name, where it cannot be proved.
3. **The previous tool from the previous operations.** Today the previous tool is entered by hand and trusted (the path says so in a note). The issue also asks for "from previous operations": the cleared area measured from the stock the earlier operations of the setup leave, including their depth - a rest pass must not assume a depth the roughing never reached. Where the carried stock cannot be established, refuse by name or mark incomplete; never guess.
4. **Zigzag.** Refused by name in the first slice because rows leave cusps along the walls of a rest area. A row plan with a closing ring per rest area would lift the refusal.

Literature to start from (cited in the first slice): Held, "On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining", LNCS 500, 1991; Veeramani and Gau, Computer-Aided Design 29(12), 1997, and IIE Transactions 32, 2000; Yao, Gupta and Nau, Computer-Aided Design 35(9), 2003. No code or text from any other CAM product (Clean-Room Protocol).

Done means: each of the four is either built with its pinning tests (verifier clean, no rapid into material the cleared-area reading cannot prove cut, refusals named) or split into its own issue with a recorded decision; the literature used is cited in the PR.

title: A rotated work offset is display-only: toolpath and machining planes stay in world axes (#315 step 3)

body:
**What happens**

The 3-2-1 alignment (#187) and `SetWcsOrigin` can set a rotated work offset, and the viewport shows the rotated frame — but nothing downstream machines in it:

- Toolpaths generate in world axes; only the offset's translation (`wcs_context` → `OriginX/Y/Z`) reaches the record stream (`posting_wcs_rotation.rs`).
- Heights / machining planes stay world-Z.
- The post refuses a rotated offset by name (#315, shipped in v0.15.0) — correct and safe, but by then the user has built a state the whole page presented as valid: the display shows a frame the CAM does not machine.

User-reported on main 5fd45923: align a setup's WCS with 3-2-1 on a turned part → the WCS is right in the display, toolpath and machining plane do not follow. Not yet pinned by a test.

**Fix (step 3 of #315, owed)**

Carry the rotation end-to-end, as a user parameter with a default:

- generation and heights compute in the offset's frame, so toolpath and machining planes follow the alignment, and
- the post either bakes rotated coordinates into the program or emits the control's own rotation where the machine declares it (Fanuc G68 / G68.2, Siemens CYCLE800 / ROT, Heidenhain PLANE / CYCL 10 — public control documentation only; a G54 register is translation only on every control).

Interim, if the full carry is not taken at once: the 3-2-1 flow should say at alignment time that a rotated offset will not post (the refusal currently arrives only at the post gate), or steer to part alignment (#330, #746).

**Done means**

A part aligned with a rotated work offset machines in that frame: toolpath, height planes and posted program all carry the same rotation, pinned against a hand-computed program — or the alignment refuses with a clear message before any toolpath exists. Never a display that shows a frame nothing machines.

**Related**: #315 (the shipped refusal), #187 (3-2-1 alignment), #330 / #746 (part alignment, the alternative path), #701 (will create rotated offsets from feature roles and needs this to machine them).

body:
Requested by the maintainer; sibling of #743 (tool and holder bodies as spun profiles).

## Two fixture variants
A fixture is one of:
- **Spun body** (turning: chucks, jaws, collets, faceplates): a half-profile on a centreline, revolved about the spindle axis. The same representation as #743's tool and holder bodies, and the same profile code.
- **Extruded profile** (milling: vises, jaws, parallels, step blocks): a closed 2D profile and an extrusion depth (along a chosen axis), placed in the setup.

## Import paths
- **From DXF.** A spun fixture is a centreline plus a half-profile, like #743. An extruded fixture is a closed profile plus the extrusion depth (entered on import, or from a DXF annotation/layer if present). Editable afterwards the way the half-profile is.
- **From STEP.** Imported as a solid and **kept and saved as STEP** in the fixture library (not converted to a profile): the fixture case keeps the vendor solid. A spun or extruded profile can optionally be derived from it, but the STEP stays the source.
- DXF read/write is shared with #743 (our own, from the published DXF reference: `LINE`, `ARC`, `LWPOLYLINE`, layers), with named refusals for unsupported entities and open or self-crossing profiles.

## Collision and simulation
- Spun and extruded fixtures are meshed for the fixture laws and the simulation from their exact profiles, so a profile edit changes what is checked and drawn.
- A STEP fixture keeps today's mesh path.

## Related
- #743: tool and holder bodies as spun profiles (shares the profile/DXF code).
- #339: handle fixtures and vises (umbrella); #561/#566 (locate the part in a fixture); the fixture library (`fixture_library`, #339); #723 (fixture_library test on Windows).

## Done means
- A spun fixture imports from a DXF half-profile and an extruded fixture from a DXF closed profile plus a depth. Both are tested: the meshed body matches the profile, and malformed input gives a named error, not a panic.
- A STEP fixture imports, saves to the fixture library as STEP, and re-inserts unchanged (test).
- The fixture laws and the simulation use the profile-built bodies (existing fixture suites pass; a new test checks a vise jaw built from a profile is hit by a rapid through it).

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
